messages.subject: Pruning neurons
parts:
Dear Zhihao,

On 24 Dec 2015, at 06:01, Zheng, Zhihao <zhen...@janelia.hhmi.org> wrote:

I am a student in Davi's lab. I have been playing with some of your R code and the nat toolbox.

Glad this is looking useful for you. Where possible could you write to nat-user Google group so that the discussion can be useful for others in future. I have cced the user group this time but feel free to write me again directly if you need to share some specific code/data that is not ready for public consumption. 

. This involves pruning the neuron, before I can scale it and resample it like you did with whole neurons.

The strategy you chose is one option and perhaps the most scaleable one, but you might also want to look at using a spatial constraint, which is very quick in interactive use. For example you can 

1. plot3d the neurons 
2. use the select3d function to draw box around the peduncle. 
3. Use nlapply(myneuronlist, subset, myselectionbox))

Anyway returning to your strategy:

1. First of all install the latest version of nat from GitHub.
2. Look at prune.neuron and subset.neuron which are newish additions

After trying out several different strategies, I settled on to do it as follows (attached is my script):
1. convert the neuron into ngraph object
2. do dfs search on the ngraph object from the tag
3. delete all non-pedunculus nodes with igraph, which turns it into a igraph object.
4. to convert igraph into a neuron, I try to make a data.frame from igraph and massage the data.frame with proper column names ('PointNo','Label','X','Y','Z','W','Parent')

Don't do this, but instead just use the function as.ngraph to turn the igraph object. 

5. use as.neuron to build a neuron from the data.frame object

You can then use as.neuron to turn the ngraph back into a neuron. You may want to specify the origin of the neuron. 

Step 1-4 seems to work fine, while step 5 causes a fatal error that aborts the whole session.

I have never seen that, but that is bad. If you have some reproducible steps can you file a bug report at GitHub. 

Something I did inappropriate? Or generally would you illuminate a proper way to prune a neuron? The system told me the prune.neuron function has not been implemented.

I also found this (line427, https://github.com/jefferis/nat/blob/94c8cf3937e7c61e8dccb7155780fad77f2c8bda/R/ngraph.R), it would be nice if prune_vertices works. But it seems as.ngraph() can't be used on an igraph object.

Thank you and happy holiday,

And you! 

Best,

Greg.
